0.content:
Albedo, Chief Alchemist of the Knights and captain of the Investigation Team, is Sucrose's teacher and superior. She calls his method "where alchemy meets art" and says that if they did the same research she would spend her whole life catching up. Even so, she chose bio-alchemy because her dreams differ from his, not to avoid competing with him. He finds working with her pleasant and sincerely enjoys teaching her. He wishes she would stop calling him "Mr. Albedo", since they are hardly generations apart. He says he more or less understands why she is so devoted to bio-alchemy. He once ordered her to take a seven-day holiday after a five-day experiment left her near collapse.

In 1.2 she told the Traveler he was "a true gentleman" who would surely repay their help, and sent them to find him on Dragonspine. In a 1.2 limited event she even recruited the Traveler to uncover his "secret", which turned out to be a strange sword. Before his trial in 5.6, Albedo told her the truth about his origin in the library. She said she was not afraid but amazed: "I trust in knowledge and science. And I trust in Mr. Albedo as a person."

At the trial (Crimes One and Two) Kaeya called her as Albedo's alibi witness: she had reviewed her research with him in the library until morning. Pressed, she could not say she had stayed awake, and Albedo gently admitted she fell asleep after midnight. He told her she did not have to lie for him. When his intercepted letter was read out she could hardly believe it, until Albedo exposed a double wearing his face. Later he warned her to retreat if things got too dangerous and leave the front line to others.

1.content:
Timaeus is Albedo's other student and runs the alchemy stall by Mondstadt's crafting bench. He calls her extremely talented for her age, a credit to Mondstadt, and luckier than him to have Albedo's appreciation, but thinks her research is a little antiquated and rarely practical. She is gentle but blunt with him: she once wondered aloud whether his research was so boring that Albedo "finally snapped", and told him his ice-crystal device needed more originality. The two of them, with Albedo, meet at the stall now and then to share their progress.

During Windblume's Breath (3.5, limited event) she quietly did his leftover work while he wrote to Ying'er, a perfumer in Liyue who had helped with his potion research. He then joined her quest to help Collei. In the 2025 birthday letter, Albedo invited Durin into the research group she and Timaeus work in.

2.content:
Sucrose met Collei, a shy trainee Forest Ranger from Sumeru, during Windblume's Breath (3.5, limited event). That year the Knights had chosen Sucrose as Windblume Festival Special Ambassador by spinning an empty Angel's Share bottle, and she was collecting "Breaths of Joy" in test tubes from people she helped. Collei wanted to find a prophecy's "blessing" and wished for "a better personality". Sucrose saw herself in her and helped her solve the riddles. She offered "a flower that is not of this world" (a Tetratanic Sweet Flower) and told Collei that her "issues" were not really issues at all. She cited her own mother: it is never too late to learn something good for you.

They kept in touch; Sucrose sent Collei's team a juicer, which Faruzan loves. In 6.6 Collei wrote that she was now an official Forest Ranger and came to Mondstadt with Tighnari, Cyno and the Traveler, and with Nicole present said goodbye to her "old self" at Windrise. Sucrose brought Amber along and wondered if, up in the sky, that old self had friends waiting "with test tubes, flasks, and bows".

3.comment: Sucrose: Diona and the ear question
3.content:
Curious whether she and the Cat's Tail bartender Diona shared ancestry, Sucrose was too worried about touching a sensitive subject to ask, because she dislikes attention to her own ears. Instead she watched Diona for a month. Diona felt stalked and was not pleased. Sucrose's note concluded: similar genome, different ancestry, "cat connection merits further study", no bone sample yet. Afterwards she made herself cat-ear glasses, which she wears only alone in her room.

By 5.4 the two trade: Diona collects bones for her (bird bones, a samachurl's staff, boar ribs, baby teeth of a wolf or dog). In exchange Sucrose gives her plants for bait, such as a Valberry bred to taste like carrot, and asks for the results. She asks after Diona's father Draff and wishes him a quick recovery.

4.content:
As a child, Sucrose and her two best friends loved a storybook about an undiscovered domain with pink flowers as tall as a hundred people, tiny fairies and perfect unicorns. They promised to reach it together. One friend left on a long journey with her adventurer parents and never returned. The other lost her father to illness, changed completely and broke off the friendship. Sucrose has no idea where they are or whether they remember her. Soon after, she read about alchemy and realised she could create the paradise herself. That is the secret purpose of her bio-alchemy. She tells the Traveler it is childish, but she still believes in fairy tales, and perhaps her friends will return once the paradise is real.

Species chosen for the paradise must meet strict standards and get a "pass" tag. In the Serenitea Pot she admits she once wanted to invite the Traveler to her private paradise but cannot build it yet, so she keeps their chosen objects in a crystal ball.

5.comment: Sucrose: Witch's Homework - The Law of Boundaries
5.content:
Albedo passed Sucrose a "task" from the Hexenzirkel: brew a potion that makes Sweet Flowers grow to sixteen times normal size ("Botanical Augmentation Reagent Type IV, Iteration VII"). Six attempts had produced a flawless potion, yet each time the flowers withered into liquid at twelve to fourteen times their size. She explained that this was the point. Alchemy follows "As above, so below", and the world has a "specification" etched into its law; repeating a failure proves the limit still exists. With the Traveler and Paimon she gathered Eye of the Storm fragments at Windrise and Springvale spring water, asked to watch the Traveler brew, and dosed flowers on Dragonspine. A Whopperflower absorbed the potion and grew at least sixteen times larger before they defeated it.

She drew no firm conclusion. Perhaps the world's limits are changing for an unknown reason, perhaps the brewer or the plant was special. From an alchemist's view, wider boundaries mean more possibilities. She warned Paimon that drinking the serum might make her sixteen times bigger or turn her into a plant-based lifeform. She explained that she studies Sweet Flowers and Sunsettias because they are sweet, and promised Paimon sugar from the Whopperflower nectar. Gameplay: completing the quest makes her a Hexerei character (Sevenfold Transmutation). The Witch's Homework is permanent content.

6.content:
At Albedo's trial for murder during the Windblume Festival, Sucrose was his alibi witness and insisted he could never be so cruel, but could not swear she had stayed awake. The real culprits, spawn of the dead dragon Durin's life force, were exposed, and monsters from Dragonspine attacked the city. Sucrose stayed at the crafting bench. Diluc and Kaeya cleared the first wave with her (she warned Kaeya that Diluc was leaving him in the dust), and she began brewing potions for the fighters. Albedo told her to retreat if needed.

At Rosaria's request Deacon Dahlia came to keep her company. Sucrose said she wasn't brave enough for this, and was shocked to hear Albedo had told close members of his order the truth long before. Dahlia told her it changed nothing. She noticed there were no wind currents nearby; Dahlia remarked that otherwise their talk would have carried across the city, which mortified her. She appears in the final scene as Durin is reborn.

7.content:
In Lohen's Story Quest (A Knight's Merit) Sucrose was debugging the "Simulation Training Bubble: Type 02". The Investigation Team had adapted the memory bubble Alice built for the Homeward welcome to recreate formidable foes from veteran knights' memories as safe training. She admitted they still did not fully understand Alice's magic and struggled to balance realism with safety. Lohen took over testing from the medic Theodore, with Adorno supplying memories. When a memory spiralled out of control she asked the Traveler to help stabilise it.

Afterwards she checked the bubble: its parameters were normal. The anomaly was a power Lohen released that was neither ordinary elemental energy nor the "Void Realm energy" Albedo speaks of. She refused to treat it as an accusation: "We shouldn't accuse our companions of anything untoward, not without evidence." She knew of the child-kidnapping rescue that earned Adorno the title "Benevolent Knight", but had never guessed Lohen was involved.

8.comment: Sucrose: Eula and the reconnaissance device
8.content: Worried that scouting was too dangerous for Eula, Sucrose built her a device to infiltrate Abyss Order camps without going in herself. Eula's imposing manner made her so nervous that she left out important details in the explanation. The device exploded, blew Eula's cover and left her facing thirteen mitachurls. Eula marched back for revenge, saw a panicked Sucrose posting the result on the wall marked "Fail", and could not go through with it. Sucrose still hopes Eula does not hold a grudge.

9.comment: Sucrose: Klee and the safe Jumpy Dumpty
9.content: Sucrose sighs that Jean has put Klee in solitary confinement many times without much introspection resulting. She promised Klee a bouncing, dancing Jumpy Dumpty that is also safe, then offered one that runs as well as jumps. Klee wants hundreds for every street in Mondstadt; Sucrose admits the design still has many problems. In 6.4 she relayed Varka's request for more Boom Blossom Bombs outside Klee's confinement room.

10.content: Jean: strict and scary to Sucrose, though she knows Jean is good; Sucrose sends Albedo in her place. Jean calls her a rare talent with a bright future (and then trails off mid-thought). Lisa: gives advice on the core of research she has never seen; Sucrose wonders whether by observation or ratiocination. Kaeya: she cannot tell his jokes from the truth. Noelle: once moved three boxes back into the lab that Sucrose had just set outside. In 3.1 (limited) the two bred the "Epsilon-Series Tetrasweet Sunsettia, Variation 63" for Razor's Weinlesefest wine. Sucrose is not a knight; at Windblume 3.5 she noticed everyone on patrol was a knight except her and Collei.

11.content:
Collecting skeletons is her passionate hobby. Every three days at dusk she visits the butcher, the Adventurers' Guild and the Springvale hunters, stammering out requests for the freshest bones "with the blood and meat still on". People found it bizarre at first, but now save rare finds for her, and she bows over and over to thank Katheryne. When she overheard a mother threatening her child with a scary old lady who carries off children's bones in a cloth sack, she investigated, was relieved to learn the story predated her, and switched to a leather sack.

Her birthday letters invite the Traveler to collect peculiar bones on her day off and to visit Liyue's wilds for the bone shards Geovishap hatchlings hoard. Everything else found is theirs, as long as she gets the shards and the data.

12.content: Limited-time event appearances, canon but not universally known. The Chalk Prince and the Dragon (1.2): she suspected Albedo was hiding a great alchemical secret, enlisted the Traveler, and studied his strange sword, sensing power flowing through it "like a living creature". Invitation of Windblume (1.4): she sent the Traveler to Albedo with an ancient recipe in an unknown language that she hoped was a Windblume; it yielded the Tetratanic Sweet Flower, with seeds four times the usual size. Shadows Amidst Snowstorms (2.3): at the alchemy stall she explained that alchemists keep separate research foci. Of Ballads and Brews (3.1): she told the Traveler her parents never placed expectations on her and hoped Razor could live doing what he loves. Alchemical Ascension (4.5): she set the alchemy exams for the Traveler's potion business. Homeward (6.4): after Dvalin fell in the river and broke a window of the Grand Master's office, she was in the freshly repaired office with Albedo and Jean.
